text:
Testing plays a crucial role in software development, helping teams deliver reliable products. Unit tests focus on individual functions or components, checking that each piece works correctly in isolation. Integration tests, on the other hand, verify that different parts of the system work together smoothly, catching issues that appear only when components interact.

Test-driven development (TDD) is a practice where you write a failing test first, then write just enough code to pass it, and finally refactor. This approach not only catches bugs early but also encourages clean, simple design.

Ultimately, a solid testing strategy gives developers confidence. When tests pass, you can release new versions or make changes without constant fear of breaking something. Testing transforms coding from guesswork into a dependable, evidence-based process.
